neighbours.label: describing something as decrepit or in poor physical condition (rickety, run-down, falling apart, crumbling); the same frames with new or well-kept things stay silent
fire: The old farmhouse was falling apart, with broken shutters and a leaking roof.
They rented a shabby flat above a shop with peeling wallpaper.
Grandpa still rides a rusty, rickety bicycle to the market.
The ferry was a battered old boat with torn seats and cracked windows.
The school building is crumbling, and rain drips into the classrooms.
We stayed in a dilapidated motel at the edge of the desert.
His boots were worn out and falling apart at the seams.
The village church is decaying, its stone walls covered in cracks.
quiet: The old farmhouse was beautifully restored, with new shutters and a solid roof.
They rented a bright flat above a shop with fresh white walls.
Grandpa still rides a shiny new bicycle to the market.
The ferry was a modern boat with soft seats and clean windows.
The school building is brand new, and the classrooms are bright.
We stayed in a charming motel at the edge of the desert.
His boots were polished and looked almost new.
The village church is well kept, its stone walls freshly cleaned.
